issues.failure_explanation: The proof claims that an inverse estimate combined with the L^2 bound yields $\|\nabla(\mathbf{y}_{\bar{\boldsymbol{u}}_h} - \bar{\mathbf{y}}_h)\|_{\mathbf{L}^{6/5}(\Omega)} \lesssim h^2$. This is mathematically invalid for two reasons: first, inverse estimates apply to discrete finite element functions, not to discretization errors involving the continuous Navier-Stokes solution $\mathbf{y}_{\bar{\boldsymbol{u}}_h}$; second, standard inverse inequalities lose a factor of $h^{-1}$, which applied to an $O(h^2)$ quantity would give $O(h)$ rather than $O(h^2)$. Furthermore, because $\mathbf{y}_{\bar{\boldsymbol{u}}_h}$ only possesses $\mathbf{H}^2$ regularity for $\mathbf{L}^2$ data, the gradient error $\|\nabla(\mathbf{y}_{\bar{\boldsymbol{u}}_h} - \bar{\mathbf{y}}_h)\|$ is generally at best $O(h)$, not $O(h^2)$.

failure_location.quote: Finally, using interpolation and inverse estimates, and estimate $\|\mathbf{y}_{\bar{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h}} - \bar{\mathbf{y}}_{h}\|_{\mathbf{L}^{2}(\Omega)} \lesssim h^{2}$, we obtain $\|\nabla(\mathbf{y}_{\bar{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h}} - \bar{\mathbf{y}}_{h})\|_{\mathbf{L}^{\frac{6}{5}}(\Omega)} \lesssim h^{2}$.

Bypass the estimation of $\|

Since $\mathbf{y}_{ ar{ oldsymbol{u}}_h} -  ar{\mathbf{y}}_h = \mathbf{0}$ on $\partial\Omega$, integration by parts transfers the spatial derivative onto $\mathbf{w}_h$ and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}_h$, bounding this term directly by $C \|\mathbf{y}_{ ar{ oldsymbol{u}}_h} -  ar{\mathbf{y}}_h\|_{\mathbf{L}^2(\Omega)} (\|\hat{\mathbf{z}}_h\|_{\mathbf{L}^\infty(\Omega)} + \|
abla \hat{\mathbf{z}}_h\|_{\mathbf{L}^4(\Omega)}) \|
abla \mathbf{w}_h\|_{\mathbf{L}^2(\Omega)} \lesssim h^2 \|
abla \mathbf{w}_h\|_{\mathbf{L}^2(\Omega)}$, which directly yields $\|
abla(\hat{\mathbf{z}}_h -  ar{\mathbf{z}}_h)\|_{\mathbf{L}^2(\Omega)} \lesssim h^2$ without differentiating the error.
issues.overall_effect: The derivation of the bound $\|\nabla(\hat{\mathbf{z}}_h - \bar{\mathbf{z}}_h)\|_{\mathbf{L}^2(\Omega)} \lesssim h^2$ in the proof of Theorem 4.3 is unestablished as written. If the gradient term were only $O(h)$, the subsequent estimate via the inverse inequality $h^{-1/2}\|\nabla(\hat{\mathbf{z}}_h - \bar{\mathbf{z}}_h)\|_{\mathbf{L}^2(\Omega)}$ would yield $O(h^{1/2})$ instead of $O(h^{3/2})$, degrading the convergence rate of the control in Theorem 4.3 and the optimal state in Corollary 4.4.
issues.title: Invalid inverse estimate on continuous-discrete state error to bound gradient in L^{6/5}
issues.why_classification: A standard, local integration by parts in the trilinear form directly bounds the dual norm by $O(h^2)$, avoiding any need to bound the gradient of the discretization error and preserving Theorem 4.3 and Corollary 4.4 without weakening any claim or rate.
